release_review.summary: Redeven v0.11.0 keeps managed Runtime lifecycle in Desktop's direct Local, SSH, or container coordinator, prepares one verified Runtime archive for Update and Reinstall, and separates Desktop-private loopback access from optional public HTTPS/WSS access at compatibility epoch 9.
checked_surfaces: Redeven consumes published github.com/floegence/floret/v5 v5.0.8 with GOWORK=off and exact module checksums; final provider usage crosses the attempt-scoped event boundary into canonical whole-thread cache token totals without a downstream ledger; Floret-native web_fetch owns secure public-text fetching, parsing, output policy, and typed Activity while Redeven owns current product authorization and UI; runtime startup atomically converges the exact legacy UTF-8 tool-result Raw representation and preserves public authority-corruption classification, canonical Effect results converge from one committed entry with valid UTF-8 text, bounded journal checkpoints preserve active-turn recovery, published SQLite maintenance reclaims eligible free pages before the single runtime open, root inventory supplies summary-only list projection, cumulative typed Activity preserves terminal call descriptions through results and restart, user Stop atomically records a terminal aborted turn and seals late provider, tool, save-point, and effect-retry work, canonical terminal items replace stream-only text without appending run-level output, stale canonical snapshots cannot replace a newer terminal view, canonical queue and interaction acceptance precedes visible success, unknown effect retries claim the stable source once unless cancellation has already won, delete and shutdown fence active subtrees and effect dispatch, migration v2 through v5 remains atomic and fail-closed, ordered views stay monotonic across live updates and restart, and no replace, go.work, sibling source path, copied contract, internal import, or Floret schema access exists
Floret ThreadService is the only lifecycle boundary for View, Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, RetryEffect, PromoteQueued, and Subscribe
Each Floret thread has one in-memory ThreadRuntime owner; its canonical journal is the only durable lifecycle fact source
Redeven persists only product settings, authorization audit, uploads, read state, and the contiguous v1-to-v2 migration import boundary
Redeven handlers authorize and map typed requests without admission receipts, authority barriers, recovery handles, or projection mirrors
Flower uses one workspace SSE, summary/detail-separated ThreadCache, ComposerDraftStore, short-lived IndexedDB TransportOutbox, and LiveTransport
Thread selection never owns execution or reconnects transport; summary updates never overwrite typed detail
Unknown irreversible tool effects are not replayed automatically and remain recoverable only from their original tool row

Redeven consumes only published Flowersec Go and Core v3.2.0 plus Floe Webapp v0.46.2, with exact module checksums, one resolved npm version across Desktop, Env App, and Code App, and no replace, file, link, workspace, portal, sibling checkout, private import, or copied transport implementation

Public Local UI uses independent HTTPS and Flowersec WSS listeners with exact Host and Origin admission, one-shot artifacts, isolated concurrent windows, explicit terminal failure, and cleanup of pending authorization, handlers, sessions, and notification sinks; the private Desktop document bridge instead uses the isolated flowersec-private-loopback/1 browser and Go APIs behind exact numeric-loopback and per-process bridge-token admission

Each remote or local accepted session registers the final Flowersec SessionHandlers, RPC, ByteStream, and terminal/live_v1 boundaries directly; outbound terminal notification sinks attach to the established Flowersec RPC peer and detach idempotently when that session ends

Desktop attach and start, CA-free private bridge health, optional public device CA trust, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, SSH runtime bootstrap, independent public WSS, terminal history recovery, and consecutive Desktop bridge sessions remain covered by focused transport contracts

Flowersec ConnectionController remains the only reconnect owner; secure-session retry uses Floe Webapp replaceConnection so an old asynchronous close cannot overwrite a new controller generation, while Redeven supplies artifact acquisition, authorization, permissions, product RPC handlers, and post-session business recovery without a second reconnect state machine or alternate carrier path

Runtime Service protocol_version is redeven-runtime-v2 at compatibility_epoch 9; Desktop verifies Runtime Service, the private bridge, Catalog, Local UI, package identity, and a unique managed process before a direct lifecycle operation succeeds
Gateway is an optional access component and never prepares, starts, stops, updates, reinstalls, or supervises a managed Runtime
